title: Collecting baskets (Ditlatlana)
text: Used to collect grains and wild fruits.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 6–7

title: Storage baskets
text: Used to store grains such as maize, millet and sorghum.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 8–9

title: Storage basket/granary (Sesigo)
text: Used to store grains such as maize, millet and sorghum. It is normally mounted on a platform of sticks to avoid invasion by pests.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 10

title: Itundu basket
material: Basketry · Woven plant fibre, cow dung
text: Used to store grain. It is covered with cow dung to protect it against insect attack.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 11

title: Winnowing tray (Leselo)
text: Used to separate the chaff from pounded grains. Woven using the mokolwane plant.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 11

title: Beer strainer (Motlhotlho)
text: Used to sieve beer and herbs.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 11

title: Fish trap (Letloa)
text: Used by Okavango communities for fishing. They vary in size according to the fish to be trapped.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 11

title: Skirt perfumer and perfume mortar (Otjihanda le Kakonzokokakora)
text: The Ovaherero dress is spread around the dome-shaped skirt perfumer. Scented herbs are burnt inside the mortar, allowing scented smoke to engulf the dress and give it a fragrant scent. Some were used for prestige and others for ritual purposes.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 12

title: Straw bag and hat
text: Made of woven straw.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 12

title: Traditional broom (Lefeelo)
text: A broom made of reeds or grass, used to sweep the lelwapa.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 13

title: Reed mat (Moalo/Moseme)
text: Made of woven reed and used for sleeping and sitting. Nowadays used for decorating inside houses.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 13

title: Tsodilo pottery
text: Discovered at Tsodilo Hills and dates from around AD 1200.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 16

title: Toutswe pottery
text: Discovered at Maiphitlhwane and dates from AD 1050–1300.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 16

title: Potsherds
text: Pots and potsherds help archaeologists to determine the origins of different ethnic groups and the dating of sites.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 16

title: Clay bowl (Mogopo)
text: Made of clay and glazed. It is used to serve food.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 17

title: Cooking pot
text: Used for cooking.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 17

title: Beer/water pot (Setsaga/Tlhatlolelo)
text: Used for storing beer or water. Was also traditionally used as an incubator for premature babies.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 17

title: Beer/water pots (Dinkgwana)
text: Used for storing beer or water.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 18

title: Decorative clay pots (Dinkgwana tsa makgabisa)
text: These are glazed pots, usually made for decorative purposes.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 19

title: Stirrer (Lefetlho)
text: Used to stir mealie meal, millet, sorghum and other food that needs mixing.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 22

title: Wooden spoons (Leso/Leswana)
text: Small spoons are used for eating, while big spoons are used for stirring either traditional beer or food.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 22

title: Wooden bowl (Mogopo)
material: Wood carving · Morula or mopipi wood
text: Made of soft wood from morula or mopipi tree trunks. Used to serve a variety of foods.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 22

title: Milk container (Orumba)
text: A round milk container made of cow skin. Used by Herero women for preparing and storing ngondivi.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 23, 47

title: Milk container (Lekuka)
text: Used for the preparation and fermentation of sour milk.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 23, 47

title: Milk container (Kgamelo)
text: Used for storing milk when milking cows.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 23

title: Milk container (Karonga/Detonga)
text: A straight-sided wooden container used by the Hambukushu to store milk.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 23

title: Pestle and mortar (Motshe le Kika)
text: Traditionally, pestles work hand in hand with mortars. Pestles are used for pounding grain and biltong, and for crushing dried fruits, seeds and nuts in the mortar.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 23

title: Traditional kgotla chair (Setilo sa dikgole)
text: Kgotla chairs are made from wood and leather thongs.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 24

title: Walking sticks
text: Normally used by elderly people for balance or support when walking. Some were used for prestige and others for ritual purposes.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 24

title: Stool (Sepora)
text: Used before the introduction of kgotla chairs. They were then used by boys and elder males.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 24

title: Thumb piano (Setinkane)
text: Musical instrument traditionally played by the Basarwa and Hambukushu. Some groups attach a small gourd for better resonance.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 25

title: Drums (Moropa)
material: Wood carving · Carved wood, animal skin
text: Musical instruments used for traditional dances, ceremonies, rituals and festivals.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 25

title: Carved figurines: animals
text: These were normally carved from wood into the shapes of animals and people, in many different figures and sizes. Some were used to chase harmful spirits away from the village, whereas nowadays they are used for decoration.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 26

title: Carved figurines
text: These were normally carved from wood into different shapes and sizes and then used for decoration.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 27

title: Thatching tool
text: Used to even out the grass when thatching a hut.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 28

title: Carved dolls
text: A woman figurine used for various purposes, e.g. by a woman who has no children but wants to conceive. If a woman should die without having borne children, a doll is buried with her to give her a better fortune in the next life.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 28

title: Snuff box
text: Used to store snuff.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 28

title: Ostrich eggshell (Lee la Ntshe)
text: Broken eggshells are used for beadwork. Ostrich eggshells are used as water containers by the nomadic !Kung of the Kalahari.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 31

title: Necklaces, tie and earrings (Dibaga le Manyena)
material: Beadwork · Ostrich eggshell and glass beads
text: Made of beads and ostrich eggshell.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 32

title: Aprons (Makgabe)
material: Beadwork · Ostrich eggshell and glass beads
text: Made of ostrich eggshell and usually worn by young women.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 33–34

title: Cosmetic bags (Kgetsana ya dinkgisa monate)
text: Used by Basarwa women to keep cosmetics.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 34

title: Waist, wrist and head bands (Maseka)
material: Beadwork · Ostrich eggshell and glass beads
text: Made of ostrich eggshell beads. Worn as normal regalia or for ceremonial purposes.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 35

title: Bellows (Moubelo)
material: Iron smelting and blacksmithing · Wood, leather
text: Bellows are used for heating charcoal when forging iron.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 37, 39

title: Metal tools (Didirisiwa tsa tshipi)
material: Iron smelting and blacksmithing · Iron, wood
text: Iron was smelted and shaped into blades used to make various household, farming and hunting tools.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 38–39

title: Leather scraper (Lengwaelo/Mokwaipo)
text: Used to scrape off bits of meat and fat and smooth the animal skin before treatment and softening.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 38

title: Blades
text: Iron was smelted and shaped into blades used to make various household, farming and hunting tools.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 39

title: Leopard skin (Letlalo la Nkwe)
text: Traditional regalia placed on the shoulders of the Kgosi during his inauguration. It carries a lot of symbolism: it makes the Kgosi appear regal and shows his dignity and bravery as tribal leader.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 41

title: Dancing skirt, apron and cloak
text: Symbolises traditional Tswana wear, but is now used by traditional dance troupes. The skirt is wrapped around the back, covering the torso, with the loin apron at the front. The cloak is fastened around the shoulders.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 42

title: Leather mat, cloak and blanket (Phate, Mokobolwane)
material: Leather · Goat, springbok and sheep skin
text: Used to keep warm during cold periods. Usually made from goat, springbok and sheep skins.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 43

title: Leather trousers, shirts and hat (Borokgwe, Hempe le Hutshe)
text: A modern style of dress, made of soft tanned skin stitched by machine into contemporary patterns and styles.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 44

title: Leather trousers (Mongato)
text: Made from animal skin with its fur removed. Sinew binding is used to stitch the trousers.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 45

title: Loin cloth (Tshega)
text: Worn by boys before puberty. The flap of skin covers the front and the leather thongs pass between the legs. Used by traditional Tswana groups, particularly the Basarwa.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 45

title: Baby sling (Thari)
text: Used by Basarwa women to carry a baby securely on the back. Made from calf skin because of its softness and durability.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 45

title: Cloak/carrying bag
text: The cloak is used for carrying roots, melons or household goods on the back. Used by Basarwa groups.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 45

title: Whip (Seme)
text: Used to whip yoked animals pulling wagons or sledges.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 45

title: Water container (Kgetsi ya Metsi)
text: Used to store water and keep it cool, especially during long trips.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 46

title: Leather preservative (Tshitlo)
material: Leather · Animal brain, fat, tree sap
text: Used to soften and preserve leather. It is a mixture of animal brain matter, fat and hardened tree sap.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 46

title: Shield and spear (Thebe le Segai/Chaka)
text: Used as weapons and for protection during fighting.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 46

title: Medicine bag and divining bones (Kgetsi ya Ditaola)
text: Used by traditional healers to store divining bones.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 46

title: Leather purse
text: Used by women to carry cosmetics and personal belongings.
catalogue: Art and Crafts of Botswana, p. 46
